^A.summary: Picks the font, rotation and size for the next text field. Use it right before ^FD so the text prints in the font you want instead of the default.
params: Font name: A to Z or 0 to 9
Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270

^A@.summary: Selects a font by its file name in printer memory instead of by a one-letter name. Use it for downloaded or custom fonts.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Drive, font name and extension, e.g. R:FONT.TTF

^B0.summary: Creates an Aztec 2D bar code. It is the same as ^BO and takes the same parameters.
params: Orientation: N, R, I or B
Extended channel interpretation code: Y or N
Error control and symbol size, 0 is the default
Menu symbol indicator: Y or N
Number of symbols for structured append: 1 to 26
Optional ID field for structured append

^B1.summary: Creates a Code 11 bar code, a numeric symbology that also encodes the dash. Used mainly for labeling telecom equipment.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Check digit: Y for one digit, N for two
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^B2.summary: Creates an Interleaved 2 of 5 bar code, a compact numeric code that needs an even number of digits. Common on cartons and shipping cases.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N
Calculate and print a Mod 10 check digit: Y or N

^B3.summary: Creates a Code 39 bar code, which encodes uppercase letters, digits and a few symbols. Widely used in industry and government labeling.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Mod 43 check digit: Y or N
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^B4.summary: Creates a Code 49 bar code, a stacked multi-row symbology that fits a lot of data in a small space.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Height multiplier of each row, in dots
Interpretation line: N none, A above, B below
Starting mode: 0 to 5, or A for automatic

^B5.summary: Creates a USPS Planet Code bar code, used on mail pieces to track them through the postal system.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^B7.summary: Creates a PDF417 bar code, a stacked 2D symbology that holds large amounts of text or binary data. Common on ID cards and shipping labels.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Height of each row, in dots
Truncate the right row indicators: Y or N

^B8.summary: Creates an EAN-8 bar code, the short retail product code used on small packages. Pass 7 digits and the printer adds the check digit.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^B9.summary: Creates a UPC-E bar code, a zero-suppressed version of UPC-A for small retail packages.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N
Print the check digit: Y or N

^BA.summary: Creates a Code 93 bar code, a denser alternative to Code 39 that can encode the full ASCII set.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N
Print the check digit: Y or N

^BB.summary: Creates a CODABLOCK bar code, a stacked symbology built from rows of Code 39 or Code 128.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Height of each row, in dots

^BC.summary: Creates a Code 128 bar code, a dense symbology that encodes all ASCII characters. It is one of the most common bar codes on shipping and logistics labels.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N
UCC check digit: Y or N
Mode: N none, U UCC case, A automatic, D UCC/EAN

^BD.summary: Creates a UPS MaxiCode, a fixed-size 2D symbol with a bullseye center used for package sorting.
params: Symbol number for structured append: 1 to 8

^BE.summary: Creates an EAN-13 bar code, the standard retail product code outside North America. Pass 12 digits and the printer adds the check digit.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^BF.summary: Creates a MicroPDF417 bar code, a smaller variant of PDF417 for moderate amounts of data.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Height of each row, in dots
Mode (columns, rows and error correction): 0 to 33

^BI.summary: Creates an Industrial 2 of 5 bar code, an older numeric symbology. It is not very dense, so it is mostly used where existing systems require it.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^BJ.summary: Creates a Standard 2 of 5 bar code, a simple numeric symbology.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^BK.summary: Creates an ANSI Codabar bar code, a numeric code with letter start and stop characters. Used by libraries, blood banks and parcel services.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N
Start character: A, B, C or D
Stop character: A, B, C or D

^BL.summary: Creates a LOGMARS bar code, a Code 39 variant used by the U.S. Department of Defense.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^BM.summary: Creates an MSI bar code, a numeric symbology used mainly for shelf labels and inventory.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Check digit selection: A none, B one Mod 10, C two Mod 10, D Mod 11 and Mod 10
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N
Show the check digit in the interpretation line: Y or N

^BO.summary: Creates an Aztec 2D bar code, a square symbol with a bullseye center. It needs no quiet zone and is common on transport tickets.
params: Orientation: N, R, I or B
Extended channel interpretation code: Y or N
Error control and symbol size, 0 is the default
Menu symbol indicator: Y or N
Number of symbols for structured append: 1 to 26
Optional ID field for structured append

^BP.summary: Creates a Plessey bar code, an older numeric symbology used for shelf and inventory labels.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print the check digit: Y or N
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^BQ.summary: Creates a QR Code. The field data starts with the error correction level and input mode, e.g. QA, for automatic mode at the default level.
params: Error correction: H, Q, M or L

^BR.summary: Creates a GS1 DataBar (formerly RSS) bar code. These compact symbols carry GTINs and extra data on small retail items such as produce.
params: Orientation: N, R, I or B
Bar code height, in dots (some types only)
Segment width for RSS Expanded: even number 2 to 22

^BS.summary: Creates a UPC/EAN 2-digit or 5-digit add-on symbol. Place it next to a UPC or EAN bar code for things like magazine issue numbers.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^BT.summary: Creates a TLC39 bar code, a Code 39 symbol combined with a MicroPDF417 symbol. It is used in the telecommunications industry.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Code 39 wide to narrow bar ratio

^BU.summary: Creates a UPC-A bar code, the standard 12-digit retail product code in North America. Pass 11 digits and the printer adds the check digit.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N
Print the check digit: Y or N

^BX.summary: Creates a Data Matrix 2D bar code, a square or rectangular symbol that stores a lot of data in a small area. Common for marking parts and healthcare items.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Height of each module, in dots

^BY.summary: Sets the default module width, wide to narrow ratio and height for the bar codes that follow. Put it before a bar code command to control its size.
params: Module (narrow bar) width in dots: 1 to 10, default 2
Wide to narrow bar ratio: 2.0 to 3.0, default 3.0
Bar code height in dots, default 10

^BZ.summary: Creates a USPS POSTNET bar code, which encodes ZIP Code data on mail.
params: Orientation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270
Print interpretation line: Y or N
Interpretation line above the code: Y or N

^CC.summary: Changes the format command prefix from the caret (^) to another character. Use it when your field data needs to contain carets.
params: New caret character, any ASCII character

~CC.summary: Changes the format command prefix from the caret (^) to another character. Same as ^CC, sent as a control command.
params: New caret character, any ASCII character

^CD.summary: Changes the delimiter that separates command parameters from the comma to another character.

~CD.summary: Changes the delimiter that separates command parameters from the comma to another character. Same as ^CD, sent as a control command.

^CF.summary: Sets the default font and size for text fields that have no ^A command. Use it at the top of a label to avoid repeating ^A on every field.
params: Default font: A to Z or 0 to 9, default A

^CI.summary: Selects the character encoding used to read field data. Use ^CI28 to send UTF-8 text with accented or non-Latin characters.
params: Character set: e.g. 0 USA, 27 code page 1252, 28 UTF-8
Optional pairs that remap a source character to a destination

^CM.summary: Reassigns the letters used to refer to the printer's memory devices (B:, E:, R: and A:).

^CO.summary: Turns the font cache on or off and sets how much extra memory it gets. The cache keeps scaled font characters ready, which speeds up printing of scalable fonts.
params: Additional memory for the cache, in KB
Cache type: 0 cache buffer, 1 internal buffer

^CT.summary: Changes the control command prefix from the tilde (~) to another character.
params: New tilde character, any ASCII character

~CT.summary: Changes the control command prefix from the tilde (~) to another character. Same as ^CT, sent as a control command.
params: New tilde character, any ASCII character

^CV.summary: Turns bar code data validation on or off. When on, the printer checks that each bar code's data is valid for its symbology and prints an error message instead of a bad code.

^CW.summary: Assigns a one-letter font name to a font stored in printer memory, so ^A can refer to it. It can also replace one of the built-in font letters.
params: Font letter to assign: A to Z or 0 to 9
Drive, name and extension of the font

~DB.summary: Downloads a bitmap font to printer memory so labels can use it.
params: Drive, name and extension of the font
Orientation of the native font: N only
Dots from the top of the cell to the baseline
Width of the space character, in dots
Number of characters in the font

~DE.summary: Downloads a character encoding table (.DAT) to printer memory. Use it with ^SE to map characters for TrueType fonts.
params: Drive, name and extension of the table

^DF.summary: Saves the rest of the format to printer memory as a reusable template instead of printing it. Mark the variable parts with ^FN, then print with ^XF.
params: Drive, name and extension of the stored format, e.g. R:LABEL.ZPL

~DG.summary: Downloads a graphic image as hex data to printer memory. Print it later with ^XG or ^IM.
params: Drive, name and extension of the graphic, e.g. R:LOGO.GRF
Total number of bytes in the graphic
The image as ASCII hex, 1 bits print black

~DN.summary: Aborts a graphic download that is in progress, for example after the host sent the wrong amount of data.

~DS.summary: Downloads an Intellifont scalable font to printer memory.
params: Drive, name and extension of the font
Size of the font data, in bytes

~DT.summary: Downloads a bounded TrueType font (256 characters or fewer) to printer memory.
params: Drive, name and extension of the font
Size of the font data, in bytes

~DU.summary: Downloads an unbounded TrueType font (more than 256 characters, e.g. Asian fonts) to printer memory.
params: Drive, name and extension of the font
Size of the font data, in bytes

~DY.summary: Downloads a file such as a graphic, PNG image, or TrueType or OpenType font to printer memory. It is the general purpose download command on newer printers.
params: Data format: A ASCII hex, B binary, C compressed
File extension, e.g. G graphic, P PNG, T TrueType
Total number of bytes in the file

~EG.summary: Erases all downloaded graphics from printer memory.

^FB.summary: Turns a text field into a block of fixed width that wraps text over several lines. Use it for addresses and descriptions; \& in the data forces a line break.
params: Extra space between lines, in dots, default 0
Justification: L left, C center, R right, J justified
Hanging indent of lines after the first, in dots
^FB.example:
^XA
^FO50,50^A0N,30,30^FB400,3,0,C,0^FDThis longer text wraps onto several centered lines^FS
^XZ

^FC.summary: Sets the characters that mark date and time placeholders in field data, such as %m or %H. The printer's real time clock fills them in at print time.

^FD.summary: Holds the data for a field: the text to print or the value to encode in a bar code. It ends at the next ^FS.
params: Data to print, up to 3072 bytes

^FH.summary: Lets you write characters in field data as hex codes after an indicator character, e.g. _5E for a caret. Use it to include ^, ~ or bytes that are hard to type.

^FM.summary: Sets the positions of each symbol when a PDF417 or MicroPDF417 bar code is split into several symbols (structured append).
params: Position of the first symbol, in dots
Position of the second symbol, and so on

^FN.summary: Numbers a field so it can be filled in later. Use it in a template saved with ^DF, then supply the data with ^FN and ^FD after recalling the template with ^XF.

^FO.summary: Sets where the next field starts, measured from the label home (^LH). The position is the top left corner of the field.
params: Distance from the left edge, in dots
Distance from the top, in dots

^FP.summary: Prints the text of a field vertically or in reverse order, and can add extra space between characters.
params: Direction: H horizontal, V vertical, R reverse
Extra gap between characters, in dots, default 0

^FR.summary: Prints the field in reverse: it flips dots between black and white wherever the field overlaps something already drawn. Use it for white text on a black box.

^FS.summary: Ends a field. Every field definition, from ^FO to its data, closes with ^FS.

^FT.summary: Sets where the next field starts, like ^FO, but the position is the text baseline (bottom left) instead of the top left corner. Fields without a position continue after the previous one.
params: Distance from the left edge, in dots
Distance from the top to the baseline, in dots

^FV.summary: Holds field data like ^FD, but marks the field as variable. With ^MCN, only ^FV fields are cleared between labels, so the rest of the image is reused.
params: Variable field data, up to 3072 bytes

^FW.summary: Sets the default rotation (and justification) for fields that don't specify their own. Use it to rotate a whole label's text at once.
params: Rotation: N normal, R 90, I 180, B 270

^FX.summary: Adds a comment to the format. The printer ignores the text that follows, up to the next command.

^GB.summary: Draws a box or a line. Use a thickness equal to the height for a filled bar, or a small height for a horizontal line.
params: Line color: B black, W white

^GC.summary: Draws a circle at the field origin.
params: Line color: B black, W white

^GD.summary: Draws a diagonal line across a box of the given width and height.
params: Line color: B black, W white
Direction: R or / right-leaning, L or \ left-leaning

^GE.summary: Draws an ellipse inside a box of the given width and height.
params: Line color: B black, W white

^GF.summary: Draws a bitmap image directly from data in the format, without storing it first. This is the usual way to put a logo or image on a label.
params: Data format: A ASCII hex, B binary, C compressed binary
Number of data bytes sent (equals c for ASCII hex)
The image data, 1 bits print black

^GS.summary: Prints a special symbol: the field data letter picks which one (A registered, B copyright, C trademark, D UL, E CSA).
params: Orientation: N, R, I or B

~HB.summary: Asks a battery-powered printer to report its battery status to the host.

~HD.summary: Asks the printer to send printhead diagnostic information to the host.

^HF.summary: Sends a stored format back to the host as ZPL text, so you can see what a ^DF template contains.
params: Drive, name and extension of the stored format

^HG.summary: Sends a stored graphic back to the host as hex data.
params: Drive, name and extension of the graphic

^HH.summary: Sends the printer's configuration (the same information as the configuration label) to the host as text.

~HI.summary: Asks the printer to identify itself: it returns the model, firmware version, resolution, memory size and installed options.

~HM.summary: Asks the printer to report its RAM status: total, maximum available and currently available memory.

~HS.summary: Asks the printer for its status. It returns three strings that report things like paper out, pause, head open, ribbon out and labels remaining in the buffer.

~HU.summary: Returns the printer's ZebraNet Alert settings to the host.

^HV.summary: Sends the data of a specified field back to the host after the label prints. Used with RFID and other fields to verify what was written or read.
params: Number of bytes to return: 1 to 256
Header text to send before the data

^HW.summary: Sends a list of the objects stored in printer memory to the host.
params: Drive and name pattern to list, wildcards allowed

^HY.summary: Uploads a graphic stored in printer memory to the host.
params: Drive, name and extension of the graphic

^HZ.summary: Asks the printer to return description information, such as settings, fonts or the object directory, as XML.
params: What to return: a all, f font links, l object directory, o object data, r printer status

^ID.summary: Deletes stored objects such as graphics, fonts or formats from printer memory. Wildcards (*) are allowed.
params: Drive, name and extension of the object to delete

^IL.summary: Loads a stored image as the background of the label, starting at the top left corner. Fields added after it print on top. Use it with ^IS to build a reusable form.
params: Drive, name and extension of the stored image

^IM.summary: Places a stored graphic at the field origin, like ^XG but without magnification. It prints faster than ^XG.
params: Drive, name and extension of the stored graphic

^IS.summary: Saves the label built so far as an image in printer memory. Use it to store a form once, then load it with ^IL on later labels.
params: Drive, name and extension of the image to save
Print the label too: Y (default) or N

~JA.summary: Cancels all formats waiting in the printer's buffer, including the one printing now.

^JB.summary: Initializes (erases and formats) a flash memory device.
params: Device: A option flash, B flash card, E internal flash

~JB.summary: Resets (erases) the optional memory on printers that have it.

~JC.summary: Runs a media sensor calibration: the printer feeds labels to learn the label length and set its sensors.

~JD.summary: Turns on communications diagnostics mode. The printer prints the data it receives as hex instead of interpreting it, which helps debug what the host is sending.

~JE.summary: Turns off communications diagnostics mode started with ~JD and returns the printer to normal operation.

~JF.summary: Sets whether a battery-powered printer pauses when the battery voltage is low.
params: Pause on low voltage: Y or N

~JG.summary: Prints a graph of the media sensor readings. Use it to see why the printer misdetects labels or gaps.

^JJ.summary: Configures the auxiliary port used to connect an applicator or other external device.

~JL.summary: Sets the label length by feeding labels until the printer finds the length. Use it after changing media.

^JM.summary: Changes the printer's resolution for the formats that follow. B halves the dots per millimeter, which makes everything print larger and coarser.
params: A full resolution (default), B half resolution

~JN.summary: Makes the printhead test fatal: if the head test finds a bad element, the printer stops and reports an error.

~JO.summary: Makes the printhead test non-fatal, which is the default: the printer reports a bad head element but keeps printing.

~JP.summary: Pauses the printer and cancels the format that is printing. If more formats are in the buffer, the printer stays paused.

~JR.summary: Resets the printer as if it had been power cycled. Unsaved settings are lost.

^JS.summary: Selects which media sensor the printer uses to detect labels.
params: Sensor: A auto, R reflective, T transmissive

~JS.summary: Controls when the printer backfeeds labels after tear-off or peel-off, as a percentage before and after printing.
params: A 100% after, B 100% before, N normal, O off, or 10 to 90

^JT.summary: Sets how often the printer runs its automatic printhead test, counted in labels.
params: Number of labels between head tests: 0 to 9999

^JU.summary: Saves the current settings to permanent memory, or reloads saved or factory settings.
params: F factory defaults, N factory network defaults, R recall last saved, S save current

^JW.summary: Sets the ribbon tension on printers with adjustable ribbon tension.
params: Tension: L low, M medium, H high

~JX.summary: Cancels a format that was only partly received, for example after the host connection dropped mid-format.

^JZ.summary: Sets whether the printer reprints a label that failed because of an error such as paper out or ribbon out.
params: Reprint after error: Y (default) or N

~KB.summary: Puts a battery-powered printer into battery discharge mode to condition the battery.

^KD.summary: Selects how the date and time are shown on the configuration label and display, for printers with a real time clock.
params: 0 version number, 1 to 4 MM/DD/YY or DD/MM/YY in 12 or 24 hour time

^KL.summary: Sets the language used on the printer's display and configuration label.

^KN.summary: Sets the printer's name and description, which show up on its web page and network tools.

^KP.summary: Sets the password that protects the printer's front panel settings.

^LH.summary: Moves the label home, the 0,0 point that all field positions are measured from. Use it to shift a whole design without editing every ^FO.

^LL.summary: Sets the label length (height). Use it for continuous media, or when the printer has not detected the label size.

^LR.summary: Prints every following field in reverse, flipping black and white where fields overlap, as if each had ^FR.
params: Reverse print all fields: Y or N (default)

^LS.summary: Shifts all fields to the left by the given number of dots. Used mainly for compatibility with older printers.
params: Shift left value, in dots: -9999 to 9999, default 0

^LT.summary: Moves the whole label image up or down relative to the top edge of the label. Use it to fix vertical alignment without changing field positions.

^MC.summary: Sets whether the label image is cleared after printing. ^MCN keeps the image so the next label only redraws its ^FV fields.
params: Clear the image: Y (default) or N

^MD.summary: Adjusts print darkness relative to the current darkness setting, for the labels that follow.

^MF.summary: Sets what the printer does with the media when it powers up and when the printhead is closed, such as feed a label or calibrate.
params: Power up action: F feed, C calibrate, L length, N none, S short calibration
Head close action: same values as p

^ML.summary: Sets the maximum label length the printer searches through when it calibrates and looks for a gap or mark.
params: Maximum label length, in dot rows

^MM.summary: Sets what the printer does with a label after printing it, such as tear-off, peel-off, rewind or cut.
params: Mode: e.g. T tear-off, P peel-off, R rewind, A applicator, C cutter

^MN.summary: Tells the printer what kind of media it is using so it can find the start of each label: continuous, gap (web), or black mark.
params: N continuous, Y or W gap/notch, M black mark, A auto-detect

^MP.summary: Disables front panel functions, such as darkness or position adjustment, so operators can't change them.
params: e.g. D darkness, P position, C calibration, E enable all

^MT.summary: Selects the printing method: thermal transfer (with a ribbon) or direct thermal (heat-sensitive media, no ribbon).
params: T thermal transfer, D direct thermal

^MU.summary: Sets the units used for positions and sizes: dots, inches or millimeters. It can also convert a format designed for one resolution to another.
params: Units: D dots (default), I inches, M millimeters

^MW.summary: Turns the printhead cold warning on or off.
params: Cold warning: Y on, N off

~NC.summary: Connects to a specific printer on a shared serial (RS-485) network, selected by its network ID.
params: Network ID of the printer: 001 to 999

^NI.summary: Assigns a network ID number to the printer for use on a shared serial (RS-485) network.

~NR.summary: Makes all printers on a shared serial network transparent, so they all receive the data that follows.

^NS.summary: Changes the printer's wired network settings, such as how it gets an IP address, the IP address, subnet mask and gateway.
params: IP resolution: e.g. A all, D DHCP, P permanent

~NT.summary: Makes the currently connected printer on a shared serial network transparent.

^PF.summary: Feeds the media forward without printing (slews) by the given number of dot rows, from the bottom of the label.
params: Number of dot rows to slew

^PH.summary: Feeds a blank label to the start of the next label (the home position), as part of a format.

~PH.summary: Feeds a blank label to the start of the next label (the home position). Same as ^PH, sent as a control command.

^PM.summary: Prints the whole label as a mirror image, flipped left to right.

^PO.summary: Rotates the whole label 180 degrees. Use it when labels come out of the printer upside down relative to how you want them.

^PP.summary: Pauses the printer when it reaches this command in a format. The printer resumes when the PAUSE button is pressed or ~PS is sent.

~PP.summary: Pauses the printer after the current label finishes printing. The printer resumes when the PAUSE button is pressed or ~PS is sent.

^PQ.summary: Sets how many copies of the label to print, and optionally when to pause and how many times to repeat each serial number.
params: Labels between pauses, 0 means no pause
Copies of each serial number, default 0
Override pause count: Y or N
Cut on error label (RFID void): Y or N

^PR.summary: Sets the print, slew and backfeed speeds. Slower speeds usually give better print quality.
params: Print speed, e.g. 2 to 14 (inches per second) or A to E

~PR.summary: Reprints the last label, like the reprint signal on an applicator. Only works when reprint is enabled.

~PS.summary: Resumes printing on a printer that is paused, for example after ^PP or ~PP. It has the same effect as pressing the PAUSE button.

^PW.summary: Sets the print width of the label. Use it so content isn't cut off or placed off the label when the media is narrower than the printhead.

~RO.summary: Resets one of the printer's advanced counters, such as a user label counter or an RFID label counter.
params: Counter: 1 or 2 user counters, 3 valid RFID, 4 voided RFID

^SC.summary: Sets the serial port settings: baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits and handshake.
params: Parity: N none, E even, O odd
Handshake: X XON/XOFF, D DTR/DSR, R RTS

~SD.summary: Sets the print darkness. It does the same as the darkness setting on the front panel.

^SE.summary: Selects a stored encoding table (.DAT) used to map characters for TrueType fonts.
params: Drive, name and extension of the encoding table

^SF.summary: Makes part of a field's data count up or down on each label printed. A mask says which characters change and how, e.g. D for decimal digits and % to skip a character.
params: Mask string: D decimal, H hex, O octal, A alpha, N alphanumeric, % skip

^SL.summary: Sets how the real time clock is printed: the time when the format was received or the time each label prints.
params: S start time, T time now, or 1 to 999 seconds of tolerance

^SN.summary: Prints a serial number that counts up or down on each label. Use it in place of ^FD, with ^PQ to print a run of labels.
params: Increment, negative to count down, default 1
Keep leading zeros: Y or N (default)

^SO.summary: Sets an offset from the real time clock for the secondary or third clock, e.g. to print a best-before date 30 days ahead.

^SP.summary: Starts printing the part of the label formatted so far while the printer keeps receiving the rest. It speeds up long labels.
params: Dot row at which to start printing

^SQ.summary: Stops a ZebraNet alert from being sent.

^SR.summary: Sets the printhead resistance value, which the printer uses to adjust heat. Needed after installing a new printhead on some printers.
params: Resistance value, from the printhead label

^SS.summary: Sets the media, web and ribbon sensor values directly. Normally the printer sets these itself during calibration.

^ST.summary: Sets the date and time of the printer's real time clock.
params: Format: A a.m., P p.m., M 24-hour

^SX.summary: Sets up a ZebraNet alert, so the printer notifies a destination such as an email address when a condition like paper out occurs.
params: Condition type, e.g. paper out or ribbon out
Alert when the condition is set: Y or N
Alert when the condition clears: Y or N

^SZ.summary: Selects which version of ZPL the printer interprets: ZPL or ZPL II.

~TA.summary: Adjusts where the media stops for tear-off or peel-off, relative to the default position.

^TO.summary: Copies an object, such as a graphic or format, from one memory device to another. Wildcards (*) are allowed.

~WC.summary: Prints a configuration label that lists the printer's current settings.

^WD.summary: Prints a label listing the objects stored in printer memory, such as fonts, graphics and formats.
params: Drive and name pattern to list, wildcards allowed

^XA.summary: Starts a label format. Every label begins with ^XA and ends with ^XZ.

^XB.summary: Suppresses the feed to the tear-off or peel-off position after the label, so no backfeed is needed before the next one. Use it to print labels back to back.

^XF.summary: Recalls a format stored with ^DF. Follow it with ^FN and ^FD pairs to fill in the template's numbered fields.
params: Drive, name and extension of the stored format, e.g. R:LABEL.ZPL

^XG.summary: Prints a stored graphic at the field origin, with optional magnification.
params: Drive, name and extension of the stored graphic

^XZ.summary: Ends a label format. The printer prints the label when it reaches ^XZ.

^ZZ.summary: Puts a battery-powered printer to sleep after it has been idle for the given time.
params: Print a label at shutdown: Y or N
